question: Your extraction system processes invoices, contracts, and shipping manifests, and it outputs JSON that downstream systems consume. On a labeled validation set, the extractions show 97% overall accuracy. The operations team now proposes to end human review for high-confidence extractions. What should you do before human review is reduced?

options.text: Approve the proposal, because 97% overall accuracy on a labeled validation set shows the extractions are reliable enough for automation across all documents.
options.reason: The guide warns that aggregate accuracy metrics such as 97% overall may mask poor performance on specific document types or fields.

options.text: Add a prompt instruction asking the model to state its overall confidence for each whole document, then automate every document where the model reports high confidence.
options.reason: The guide calls for field-level confidence scores calibrated with labeled validation sets, not uncalibrated document-level self-reports, and it still skips the per-segment accuracy check.

options.text: Measure accuracy separately for each document type and each extracted field, and confirm that every segment performs consistently before reducing review.
options.reason: The guide says to analyze accuracy by document type and field to verify consistent performance across all segments before reducing human review.

options.text: Expand the labeled validation set until the overall accuracy estimate is statistically precise, then automate every extraction above the existing confidence threshold.
options.reason: A more precise aggregate figure is still an aggregate, so it can hide weak document types or fields that the guide says must be validated per segment.
